name: "Kiwi" — the New Zealand medic
role: Medic at the Núi Bà Đen camp; a New Zealander
summary: The medic Larry held sick call with on Núi Bà Đen for the Cambodian strikers and their families: "Captain Kennedy handled the political problems. Me and the medic handled the sick call." Larry called him Kiwi because he was a New Zealander, and they went down to Saigon together "probably 15 times," meeting Ron Tototz there. "I don't remember the medics name at all. Might have been Roger."
researchNotes: New on 2026-09-05 (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0041-c18308745.json), and a genuinely checkable man: New Zealand's military presence in Vietnam in 1964–65 was tiny — an engineer detachment from June 1964 and an artillery battery from July 1965 — and a New Zealander serving as a medic at a U.S. Special Forces camp in Tây Ninh would be an exception someone recorded. Two readings to keep apart: a New Zealand serviceman attached to the camp, or a New Zealand-born man in the U.S. Army (foreign nationals enlisted; the nickname would have followed him either way). The first is a search in New Zealand records (Archives New Zealand, the NZ Vietnam veterans' rolls); the second is a morning-report question like every other name here. Nothing further should be put to Larry until one of those has been tried — he has said he does not remember the name, and 'Roger' is the most he has.
